title: Xi Jinping State Visit to Pyongyang Officially Confirmed for June 8–9 — First China-DPRK Summit Since 2019
detail: China's Xinhua News Agency and the Communist Party's International Department officially confirmed on June 5, 2026 that President Xi Jinping would pay a state visit to North Korea on June 8–9, at the invitation of Kim Jong-un. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said: 'The two sides will take this visit as an opportunity to promote bilateral relations.' The Xi visit marks his first trip to Pyongyang since June 2019 — a seven-year gap — and his first overseas trip of 2026. Beijing framed the visit around the 65th anniversary of the 1961 Sino-DPRK Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance. The timing, coming immediately after Xi's back-to-back summits with Trump (May 14–15) and Putin (May 20) in Beijing, frames China as the central diplomatic broker in both the US-China-Russia triangle and the Korean Peninsula question. Strategic context: China accounts for approximately 95% of North Korea's total trade and remains the DPRK's primary diplomatic shield at the UN Security Council. The visit is broadly read as Beijing's effort to reassert influence over Pyongyang after the DPRK's deepening strategic and military alignment with Russia since 2023. During Trump's Beijing meeting in May, both leaders had stated a 'shared goal to denuclearize North Korea,' and the Xi–Kim talks are expected to include managing DPRK nuclear escalation. The announcement of the visit came one day after Kim publicly revealed a third uranium enrichment factory and pledged 'exponential' expansion of the DPRK nuclear arsenal — a signal analysts say Kim intended to send ahead of Xi's arrival, to foreclose any nuclear concession expectations. Separately, the US State Department reaffirmed on June 5 that it 'remains open to dialogue with North Korea without preconditions' and is committed to 'complete denuclearization,' in direct response to Kim's June 3 nuclear escalation speech.
